title: Quasi-compact quasi-separated zero-dimensional schemes are affine
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] that is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] and quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Suppose every point of $X$ is closed (equivalently, $X$ has topological Krull dimension at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]). Then $X$ is affine: there is a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. The empty scheme is allowed. No Noetherian or finite-type hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero: implication (1) to (2) and final assertion that a quasi-compact quasi-separated scheme of dimension zero is affine.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open] to the quasi-compact open $X\subseteq X$. Obtain a finite affine open cover $X=\bigcup_{i=1}^nU_i$, and choose presentations $U_i\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A_i$. The family may be empty when $X=\varnothing$. Every singleton in $U_i$ is closed, since it is the intersection of $U_i$ with a singleton closed in $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, opening paragraph and final paragraph: choose an affine open covering and use quasi-compactness to make it finite.

proof.text: For each $i$, every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ of $A_i$ is maximal. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak m\supseteq\mathfrak p$, which is prime. In the Zariski topology [def-weil-affine-spectrum] write the closed singleton $\{\mathfrak p\}=V(S)=\{\mathfrak q:S\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$ for some $S\subseteq A_i$. Since $S\subseteq\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak m$, we have $\mathfrak m\in\{\mathfrak p\}$, so $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak m$. Thus no closed-point/maximal-ideal correspondence is being used as an unstated lemma.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, (2) and proof of (8), together with Tag 00E1, definition-Zariski-topology; the closed-point/maximal-ideal observation in the opening of section-ring-jacobson.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-spectrum-profinite] to each $A_i$, with its all-primes-maximal hypothesis proved in step 2. Hence each $U_i$ is Hausdorff. Each $U_i$ is also quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Since $X$ is quasi-separated, [pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc] implies that $U_i\cap U_j$ is quasi-compact for all $i,j$. This is quasi-compactness in the subspace topology, in particular as a subset of $U_j$. No intersection is asserted affine at this stage.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, opening paragraph and (1) implies (2); underlying facts are Algebra Tag 04MG, lemma-ring-with-only-minimal-primes, and Schemes Tag 01KO, lemma-characterize-quasi-separated.

proof.text: Fix $i,j$ and put $K=U_i\cap U_j\subseteq U_j$. For $y\in U_j\setminus K$, Hausdorffness gives, for each $z\in K$, disjoint open neighbourhoods $V_z$ of $z$ and $W_z$ of $y$ in $U_j$. Quasi-compactness supplies $z_1,\ldots,z_r$ with $K\subseteq\bigcup_aV_{z_a}$. Then $\bigcap_aW_{z_a}$ is an open neighbourhood of $y$ disjoint from $K$. Thus $K$ is closed in $U_j$, including $K=\varnothing$ with the empty intersection equal to $U_j$. Consequently $U_j\setminus U_i$ is open in $U_j$, hence in $X$. Since the $U_j$ cover $X$, their union $X\setminus U_i$ is open. Therefore every $U_i$ is closed in $X$ as well as open. This is the finite-neighbourhood proof of compact subsets being closed in a Hausdorff space, written out from the definitions.

source.place: Tag 08YB, lemma-quasi-compact-in-Hausdorff, proof of (1); applied locally as in Properties Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero.

proof.text: For each $i$, the open inclusion $j_i:U_i\hookrightarrow X$ is an immersion: it factors as the identity closed immersion $U_i\to U_i$ followed by that open inclusion, using [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Its image is closed by step 4. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion] makes $j_i$ a closed immersion. These are the original affine open subschemes, now also closed subschemes; no induced reduced structure is substituted.

source.place: Tag 01IQ, lemma-immersion-when-closed; applied to the affine open inclusions shown closed by the local argument of Properties Tag 0CKV.

proof.text: The finitely many affine closed subschemes $U_i\hookrightarrow X$ of step 5 cover $X$ set theoretically by step 1. Apply [lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine] to this family: $X$ is affine, so there exist a commutative ring $A$ and an isomorphism $X\simeq\operatorname{Spec}A$. Its statement explicitly includes the empty family for $X=\varnothing$. This uses neither a Noetherian nor a finite-type hypothesis. It completes the finite-cover argument using the existing general closed-cover affineness lemma.

source.place: Tag 09NL, lemma-affines-glued-in-closed-affine; used after the affine charts have been proved closed by the argument of Properties Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, affine-chart argument, completed by the existing finite affine closed-cover lemma of Limits Tag 09NL rather than repeating the final clopen-partition induction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-NR-125bb0b8c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, all six steps and every cited statement in full; there are no new nodes and no changes. The statement matches Stacks Properties 0CKV (lemma-dimension-zero), final assertion: a qcqs scheme whose points are all closed is affine, the empty scheme is allowed, and there is no Noetherian hypothesis. The 'dim<=0' parenthetical is correct because X is quasi-compact. Step 1: the Mathlib leaf lem-pqf-finite-affine-cover-qc-open, applied with U=X, gives a finite affine cover (empty when X is empty). Step 2 is elementary: closed singleton {p}=V(S) and a maximal ideal m containing p (00E0 node) force m=p. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-zero-dimensional-spectrum-profinite (04MG) makes each chart compact Hausdorff, lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs makes it quasi-compact, and pqf-lem-qs-intersection-qc makes the overlaps quasi-compact; no overlap is claimed affine, so there is no E1 fault. Step 4 is elementary and written out: a compact subset of a Hausdorff chart is closed, so each U_j minus U_i is open and each U_i is closed in X. Step 5: by def-weil-closed-immersion and 01IQ (an immersion with closed image is a closed immersion), each open inclusion is a closed immersion with the original structure sheaf. Step 6: lem-sc-closed-affine-union-affine matches Limits 09NL as stated (no extra hypotheses; read in limits.tex). Its hypotheses come from steps 1 and 5, and it does not restate the item. The route differs from 0CKV's final partition induction; it is valid and marked agent-written. The dependency closure (1023 nodes) does not return to the item. The only citer, lem-sfb-field-profinite-galois-site paragraph (3), uses the all-points-closed form. No SGA source is cited, and the item is not in route-pivot-dropped.txt. I accept the off-unit tool uses for the maintainer's tool_uses: 04MG spectrum topology, the quasi-separated intersection criterion and 09NL. Note for the maintainer: lem-sc-finite-discrete-separated-affine and lem-sc-zero-dim-noetherian-affine are special cases of this item that already existed; they could later cite it. I checked small cases: Spec 0, k[eps]/eps^2, Spec of the product of F_2 over N, an infinite disjoint union of points, and a non-quasi-separated gluing of two copies of Spec(prod F_2).
